correctness.rationale: For all 1<p_i<infty and 1/q=1/p1+1/p2, the logarithmic change of variables is isometric, converts each physical window into a positive L1 convolution of exact mass A_i, and cancels the x^-2 weight in the target Lq norm. Minkowski followed by Holder gives norm <=A1 A2; normalized increasing logarithmic intervals give norm >=A1 A2. Strict convexity forbids equality in the one-input convolution bounds for a nonzero input. Dilation invariance concentrates outputs on arbitrary small initial intervals while compact bilinear images have uniformly vanishing small-set Lq tails. The powered min(1,q)-triangle inequality gives distance to every compact map >=full norm, valid for q<1, and zero map yields equality. All finite rank approximation numbers consequently equal full norm. No external computation or limit of finite experiments is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating full primary source leaves the sharp numerical norm of Example 11.2 uncomputed (it gives log 2 as upper bound), and Example 11.4 likewise supplies only a central-profile lower witness; no checked source provides the simultaneous exact all-width/all-critical-exponent formula or the nonattainment assertion. Its equality of essential distance and full norm is explicitly credited as prior; it alone does not supply the sharp constant. The standard positive-convolution norm identity and strict convexity are prior ingredients. The full theorem is a new explicit quantitative calibration relative to the inspected sources, with a documented risk of implicit classical coverage.
residual_risks: A general earlier positive-convolution norm formula and a general shift-invariant essential-norm lemma, if stated jointly at sufficient strength, could imply this theorem as an unstated corollary; failure to find one is not an originality proof.
The critical model has a short exact proof using classical Minkowski, Hölder, and translation strict convexity; it could be known informally or implicitly without published numeric evaluation.
Searches cannot exclude unpublished work, differently indexed articles, or independent simultaneous derivations.

value.rationale: The exact norm of the scale-invariant moving-window benchmark is a natural sharp invariant in the critical bounded noncompact regime; the motivating source explicitly studies it but provides only log(2) as an upper bound for its symmetric example and a lower-profile witness for its asymmetric one. The all-critical-exponent and all-fixed-window sharp formula resolves both calibrations uniformly, while proving total finite-rank approximation rigidity and nonattainment. It is not an arbitrary isolated parameter slice, numerical recomputation, or unsupported downstream claim. Limits and classical ingredients are distinguished from the quantitative contribution.
